text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Post und Telekom Austria (PTA) threatens to scrap 2,300 bus lines if provincial governments and councils will not compensate for the losses from the unprofitable routes.
- Freedom Party announces a petition for a referendum in autumn on the introduction of Europe's single currency, the euro.
- Record order intake should help lift Auricon's business results substantially.
- Lauda Air has been given the go ahead to pick up passengers in Kuala Lumpur and to fly them on to Australia.
- The ruling coalition of the SPOe and OeVP warn against holding a referendum on the euro.
- Losses on the Vienna stock exchange were not as bad as earlier feared after Wall Street racked up its second worst points fall on Friday.
- Swedish paper giant SCA has bought a minority stake of 48 percent in Austrian corrugated cardboard maker Welpa.
- The division of the postal system and the sale of postal savings bank P.S.K will be decided on in autumn next year.
- Tour operator Gulet Touristik expands fast and expects a 40 percent sales increase for the current year.

- The majority of Austrians are against holding a referendum on the introduction of the euro, an opinion poll finds. Only 33 percent of those asked thought it would make sense asking the nation to decide.
